stem: A 70-year-old man with metastatic prostate cancer has been on a monthly depot injection of leuprolide for 3 months. Initially his bone pain worsened for a few days. He is not taking any other hormonal therapy.
oneliner: 70M + metastatic prostate cancer + monthly depot leuprolide x 3 months + initial brief flare → which hormone set now?
ask: Which set of changes best describes his hormones after 3 months?

whyNot.B: This is the **first-week flare** of an agonist (or pulsatile dosing); after months the receptors are down-regulated
whyNot.C: If LH falls, Leydig cells stop stimulation, so testosterone **cannot rise**
whyNot.D: This fits **primary testicular failure** (loss of negative feedback); his pituitary is being suppressed
whyNot.E: If LH stayed normal, Leydig cells would keep making testosterone; a lasting fall needs **less LH**, which continuous agonist exposure produces

answer: LH, FSH and testosterone all fall
why: Pulsatile GnRH stimulates the pituitary, but **continuous GnRH agonist** exposure first causes a brief **flare** and then **down-regulates GnRH receptors**. **LH and FSH fall**, so Leydig cells make less **testosterone**, giving medical castration.
chain: Pituitary GnRH receptors desensitize and down-regulate

idea.rule: Continuous GnRH shuts the axis off; pulsatile GnRH drives it.
also: Pulsatile GnRH treats hypothalamic amenorrhea or Kallmann syndrome
Leuprolide for endometriosis, fibroids, central precocious puberty
Leuprolide for estrogen-dependent breast cancer: LH and FSH fall
Continuous agonist in IVF prevents a premature LH surge

stem: A 48-year-old woman has had no menstrual periods for 4 months apart from scant spotting. She reports vaginal dryness. Her weight is stable, she does not exercise heavily, and she has no breast discharge or cold intolerance. Pregnancy test is negative.
oneliner: 48F + 4 months amenorrhea + vaginal dryness + stable weight, no galactorrhea + negative hCG → which hormone change?

options.D: FSH normal, LH raised, androgens raised

whyNot.B: Raised prolactin usually causes **galactorrhea**; she has **no breast discharge**
whyNot.C: Low thyroxine brings **cold intolerance**, which she **lacks**
whyNot.D: This is **PCOS**, where estrogen is preserved; her **vaginal dryness** shows low estrogen
whyNot.E: Low FSH and LH mean **hypothalamic** amenorrhea from weight loss or heavy exercise; her **weight is stable** and she does not train hard

why: With follicles running out, **estradiol and inhibin B** fall, so the pituitary is no longer restrained and **FSH** (first and most) and LH rise. Vaginal dryness reflects low estrogen.

idea.rule: Ovarian failure shows high FSH and LH with low estradiol (loss of negative feedback).
also: Primary ovarian insufficiency before age 40 gives the same pattern
Hypothalamic amenorrhea: FSH and LH low
Inhibin B falls first and drives the early FSH rise
